title: Evals are becoming the spec: 'eval-driven development' and a first-class 'evals engineer' role are crystallizing as the way AI features get defined and shipped
summary: A pattern that was fringe a year ago is converging fast across independent practitioner sources: for AI-powered features, the evaluation suite — not the PRD or the unit-test file — is becoming the primary artifact that defines done. Braintrust's Ameya Bhatawdekar ('Evals are the new PRD', Mar 27, 2026) reframes the loop from Problem→Spec→Design→Build→Ship to Problem→Eval→Hillclimb→Ship, with the eval serving as 'the spec, the acceptance criteria, and the roadmap all at once', and quotes OpenAI CPO Kevin Weil that 'writing evals is the most important thing a PM can do in the AI era.' The corroborating signal is organizational, not just rhetorical: a distinct 'evals engineer' role — barely existent in 2023 — is now an early technical hire at applied-AI companies (Cursor, Harvey, Sierra, Decagon, Cognition) and is being staffed into evals teams at enterprises like Stripe, Shopify, and Databricks to vet third-party model use, with open reqs at Anthropic, OpenAI, and Scale. The mechanism is simple and durable: because frontier models change underneath a prompt every few weeks, a versioned eval suite that gates every PR is the only thing that catches silent regressions — so evals inherit the role tests played in deterministic software. Lead time: this is roughly 6-12 months ahead of where mainstream engineering orgs are; most still treat evals as an ML-team concern rather than a core SDLC gate and an emerging job family.
source: Braintrust blog ('Evals are the new PRD', Ameya Bhatawdekar), with corroborating role/hiring evidence
whyItMatters: For any team shipping LLM-backed features, the release gate is moving from deterministic tests to eval suites — leaders who leave evals as an informal ML-team activity will ship silent quality regressions every time a model updates underneath them.

A new job family ('evals engineer' / 'evals eng') is forming and being hired as a first-ten technical role at AI-native companies; workforce and skills planning should account for it now rather than after competitors have staffed it.

Reframing product specs as evals shifts what PMs and engineers actually do — from writing prose requirements to curating labeled failure cases — which changes hiring criteria, onboarding, and how 'done' is negotiated.
recommendedActions: Pick one AI-backed feature and require a versioned eval suite to pass in CI before merge; treat model or prompt changes as changes that must clear the same gate.
Stand up a lightweight 'eval flywheel': have PMs/engineers curate a handful of real production failures into new eval cases each week, and track eval pass-rate as a first-class release metric.
Decide deliberately whether evals ownership sits with a dedicated hire, the platform team, or product engineers — and write it into role definitions before the gap becomes an incident.
Audit third-party model usage: enterprises are spinning up evals teams specifically to vet vendor models — define the eval bar a model must clear before it touches production.
risksAndCaveats: Several anchor sources are vendors selling eval tooling (Braintrust, Vercel, FutureAGI, Scale); the practice is real but the framing carries commercial intent, and no source provides hard outcome data that EDD beats traditional methods.
The strongest evidence today is directional (job postings, practitioner essays, convergent language), not a controlled study — this is an emerging-practice signal, not a proven productivity result.
The claim is most established for teams building AI products; how far 'evals as spec' generalizes to conventional software with deterministic behavior is unproven.
observer: Ameya Bhatawdekar of Braintrust, corroborated by independent practitioner sources and evals-engineer job postings
